uncertain-dblp.license: processed graph not distributed; code: 'freely use for research purposes, provided that you acknowledge the authors' (project page); hdblp (historical dblp): ODC-BY 1.0 (TO VERIFY)
uncertain-dblp.notes: UNAVAILABLE as data (checked 2026-11-09, PR-27). Project page https://helios2.mi.parisdescartes.fr/~themisp/collectiveclassification/ (read via WebFetch; direct HTTPS from the agent session is blocked by the proxy, 403) distributes only sourcecode.zip (all algorithms, incl. xml2dat.py; research-use-only terms) and describes the graph: DBLP XML downloaded Aug 13, 2012 from http://dblp.uni-trier.de/xml/, 850,128 articles, 677,098 nodes, 4,122,556 edges, 14 labels, 153,022 labelled, 73,588 components. The paper (SSDBM 2014, arXiv:1405.5829) reports 922,673 nodes / 3,389,272 edges, 1980-2010 publications, 16% labelled, p = probability that two authors co-authored in a randomly chosen year. No graph/label files are published. The Aug-2012 dblp.xml is not offered as a release (dblp.org releases and the DROPS dblp artifacts list no 2012 data release, only DTDs); the closest rebuild route is hdblp (Zenodo record 1213051, ODC-BY 1.0), which reconstructs dblp for any day June 1999 - March 2018 'within certain limits' (blog.dblp.org 2018-07-11). Rebuilding = hdblp snapshot -> xml2dat.py -> their label rule; not implemented (substantial, and the result would be a reconstruction, TO VERIFY against the published counts).
uncertain-dblp.status: unavailable (no published data; rebuild route via hdblp identified, not implemented)

us-patent-assignee.notes: UNAVAILABLE as packaged data (checked 2026-11-09, PR-27). Dallachiesa et al. (SSDBM 2014, arXiv:1405.5829 §6): assignee graph built from the NBER U.S. Patent Citations Data File [Hall, Jaffe, Trajtenberg 2001], patents issued 1970-1990, 108,658 nodes, 1,059,822 edges, 5 NBER categories (Chemical; Computers & Communications; Drugs & Medical; Electrical & Electronic; Mechanical), label = most frequent category of the assignee's patents, 66% labelled, p = 'estimate of the probability that one of the two assignees cites the other' (example 5 of 20 citations = 0.25; exact formula not given). The authors publish no graph. Raw inputs are online: https://www.nber.org/research/data/us-patents-1975-1999 lists pat63_99.zip and Cite75_99.zip at https://data.nber.org/patents/ (not downloaded). Rebuild needs the unspecified probability formula, and Cite75_99 appears to cover citing patents of 1975-1999 only (TO VERIFY), so 1970-74 citations may be missing; not trivial, not implemented.
us-patent-assignee.status: unavailable (rebuild from NBER files possible in principle; edge-probability formula unspecified)
